terra.problem: Saying Paul is glad to acknowledge Phoebe's help gives him a feeling the text does not state.
The hot-tray joke does not clearly match the action of turning away. It is unclear why pointing his mustache would need a second opinion.
The explanation calls the quoted instruction three words, but it has four.
The cookie-appetite joke makes light of the serious self-serving conduct Paul is warning about.
Paul says smooth talk and flattery deceive people; he does not say the voice is quiet or friendly.
The burnt-dough comparison does not make the distinction between being wise about good and innocent about evil clear. Papa would also need to know about burnt cookies to recognize them.
Saying Tertius earned his greeting adds a reason for it that the text does not give.
Tertius sending greetings to the believers does not establish that he isn't their leader. The text identifies him as the one who wrote down the letter but does not state whether he leads the church.
Paul says Gaius hosted him and the whole church, but the text does not say they gathered at Gaius's place.

The guest-list and cookie-box comparison connects the nations in this verse to the Marriage Supper. The passage says the mystery is made known to lead all nations to obedience from faith, not that they are a guest list for the Supper.
The statement that Paul is an apostle needs a reference. Romans 16 does not state it.
